description.narrative:
Following the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, the General Federation of Bahrain Trade Unions (GFBTU) has been actively engaged to provide new services to migrant workers in a vulnerable situation. From April – May 2020, the GFBTU launched an online questionnaire to assess the impact of COVID-19 on migrant workers (capturing responses from 308 respondents from numerous nationalities). Based on the evidence that many workers (66 per cent) did not receive their owed wages, and many others were facing a humanitarian crisis, the GFBTU allocated internal resources to temporarily provide food and other aid. In February 2021, the GFBTU launched an initiative to strengthen the role of the Migrant Workers’ Committee (MWC), comprising 13 community representatives from 11 countries as well as a hotline and a lawyer to provide legal support (55 cases during the reporting period). In total, the GFBTU has trained more than 120 (Philippine) migrant workers on the labour law, reached more than 600 (Indian) workers, particularly in the construction and cleaning sectors, with awareness raising campaigns on OSH, focussing on heat exhaustion and other heat-related risks. Additionally, the GFBTU had a role in facilitating access to vaccination for around 3,500 Indian workers in an irregular situation who received at least one dose of the vaccine as at June 2021 (collaboration with Indian embassy). The GFBTU was actively engaged through meetings with the Minister of Labour and requested intervention to facilitate the vaccination for workers in an irregular situation. With the support of the Government of Switzerland, the ILO provided the following support to the General Federation of Bahrain Trade Unions (GFBTU): - Technical support in developing the online questionnaire to assess the impact of COVID-19 on migrant workers; - Technical advice and legal assistance for migrant workers - Technical support (in collaboration with the Building and Wood Workers’ International - BWI (a global union federation) to develop awareness raising materials for migrant workers in the construction sector).
With respective to the Migrant Workers’ Committee, this was an initiative first commenced via ILO support in October 2019, and during the current biennium, the ILO (with support of the government of Switzerland) continued to provide technical and financial support in terms of stipends, and a national coordinator to support the MWC.
